summary: Exercise the production release control flow through a scheduled non-publishing canary and report CI queue, execution, critical-path, cancellation, and retry metrics.
security: The canary writes only immutable scratch image tags and cannot advance semantic tags, latest aliases, Docker Hub, packages, charts, or GitHub releases.
The canary verifies exact ORAS digests, signatures, provenance, vulnerability evidence, and non-publisher pull access before reporting success.
documentation: Maintainer routing and artifact-promotion runbooks describe lane selection, canary evidence, rollback, OSS/plugin ownership, and p95 release targets.
Developer-workflow skills route all future work to the OSS host and independently released owning plugin repositories; standalone EE development is retired.
knownLimitations: The 45-minute release objective remains an observed rollout target until protected canary, cache, representative pull-request, and controlled patch-release evidence is collected.
rollback: Pause the scheduled canary and restore the previous cost-report workflow; scratch artifacts may expire naturally under registry retention policy.
Keep the immutable candidate workflow fail closed while investigating any canary or digest mismatch.
validation: Canary contracts verify scratch-only publication, production reusable-workflow reuse, exact digest checks, and prohibition of public package or release mutation.
Observability tests verify p50/p95 timing, runner minutes, superseded cancellation classification, retries, and workflow/job summaries.
The EnterpriseGlue developer-workflow plugin validates all versioned skills and contains no EE write or synchronization path.
